revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Puzzle Problem
revealWordProblem.text:
The percentage of each type of puzzle in a toy store before a sale is shown. During the sale, the store sold all of its 300-piece and 500-piece puzzles — 120 puzzles in all.
Question: How many of each type of puzzle did the store have before the sale?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A picture graph of puzzle stock by type: 300-piece 40%, 500-piece 35%, 750-piece 15%, and 1,000-piece 10%.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The puzzles that sold were the 300-piece and 500-piece stock together: 40% + 35% = 75% of the whole stock. So 120 is 75% of the total: 0.75t = 120, giving t = 160 puzzles before the sale. Now take each percent of 160 — 300-piece: 40% of 160 = 64; 500-piece: 35% of 160 = 56; 750-piece: 15% of 160 = 24; 1,000-piece: 10% of 160 = 16. Check: 64 + 56 = 120 sold, and 64 + 56 + 24 + 16 = 160.

turnAndTalk.question: Akela paid $42 for a sweater, and that was 60% of the original price. BEFORE computing: will the original price be more or less than $42? How do you know?
turnAndTalk.kernel: The original price is the whole (100%), and $42 is only part of it (60%), so the whole must be more than $42.

turnAndTalk.question: To find the whole when 60% is $42, one strategy finds 10% first. Why is 10% such a useful stepping stone, and how does it get you to 100%?
turnAndTalk.kernel: If 60% is $42, then 10% is 42 ÷ 6 = $7, and ten of those steps make 100%: 10 × $7 = $70.

turnAndTalk.extend: Show that the equation 0.6 × v = 42 tells the same story in one move. Where did the 10%-steps go inside v = 42 ÷ 0.6?

turnAndTalk.question: Sheng's car is worth $26,600 today, which is 70% of what his parents paid. One partner should find the price with 10%-steps on the double number line; the other with the equation 0.7v = 26,600. Compare: where does each method show the SAME division?
turnAndTalk.kernel: 10% is 26,600 ÷ 7 = $3,800, so 100% is $38,000 — and the equation v = 26,600 ÷ 0.7 = 38,000 lands on the same answer.

turnAndTalk.kernel: When the whole is unknown, divide the part by the percent; the whole must come out larger than the part whenever the percent is under 100%.

conceptIntro.heading: Determine the Whole Given the Part and Percent
conceptIntro.intro: When you know a part and its percent, you can work backward to find the whole, which is 100%.
conceptIntro.introEs: Cuando conoces una parte y su porcentaje, puedes trabajar hacia atrás para hallar el entero, que es el 100%.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Put the part and its percent in a ratio table. Scale the percent to 100% to find the whole. Check that the whole is more than the part.
conceptIntro.keyIdeaEs: Pon la parte y su porcentaje en una tabla de razones. Cambia la escala del porcentaje a 100% para hallar el entero, y comprueba que el entero sea más que la parte.

iDo.title: Example 1 · Use a ratio table
iDo.titleEs: Ejemplo 1 · Usa una tabla de razones
lines: Akela paid $42 for a sweater on sale. That was 60% of the original price. What was the original price?
Write the part and its percent in the first column: 60% : 42
Solve the same problem with an equation. $42 is 60% of the original price. Let v be the original price.
Write 60% and $42 in the first column: 60% : 42
Divide the price by 0.6 too: v = 42 ÷ 0.6 = 70
linesEs: Akela pagó $42 por un suéter en oferta. Eso era el 60% del precio original. ¿Cuál era el precio original?
Escribe la parte y su porcentaje en la primera columna: 60% : 42
Divide los dos entre 6 para hallar el 10%: 42 ÷ 6 = 7
Multiplica los dos por 10 para llegar al 100%: 7 × 10 = 70
Resuelve el mismo problema con una ecuación. $42 es el 60% del precio original. Sea v el precio original.
Escribe 60% y $42 en la primera columna: 60% : 42
Divide el precio entre 0.6 también: v = 42 ÷ 0.6 = 70

weDo.title: Let's do one together
lines: Sheng's car is now worth $26,600. That is 70% of what his parents paid for it. What did they pay for the car?
What amount goes with 70% in the first column? (26,600)
Divide both by 7. What amount matches 10%? (3,800)
What do you multiply 10% by to reach 100%? (× 10)
Do the same to the other row. What is the whole? (38,000)
Check: is the whole more than the part? (Yes. $38,000 is more than $26,600.)
linesEs: El carro de Sheng ahora vale $26,600. Eso es el 70% de lo que pagaron sus papás por él. ¿Cuánto pagaron por el carro?
¿Qué cantidad va con 70% en la primera columna? (26,600)
Divide los dos entre 7. ¿Qué cantidad va con el 10%? (3,800)
Haz lo mismo en la otra fila. ¿Cuál es el entero? (38,000)
Comprueba: ¿el entero es más que la parte? (Sí. $38,000 es más que $26,600.)

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake when finding the whole is multiplying by the percent instead of dividing. For "$42 is 60% of the original price," computing 0.6 × 42 = $25.20 makes the original price SMALLER than the sale price — impossible for a discount. Since percent × whole = part, the whole is found by dividing: 42 ÷ 0.6 = $70. Whenever the percent is less than 100%, the whole must come out larger than the part, so a smaller answer is the tell.

hints: Re-read the question. What exactly is it asking you to find?
You already HAVE the part — the question runs backward, so divide instead of multiplying.
Start like this: Write 10% as a decimal: 0.1.
parallelPractice.explanation: Write 10% as a decimal: 0.1. The part ÷ the percent gives the whole: 16 ÷ 0.1 = 160. Check: 10% of 160 = 16.
parallelPractice.stemEs: El 10% de un número es 16. Encuentra el entero (el 100%).
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la pregunta. ¿Qué te pide encontrar exactamente?
Ya TIENES la parte: la pregunta va hacia atrás, así que divide en vez de multiplicar.
Empieza así: Escribe 10% como decimal: 0.1.
parallelPractice.explanationEs: Escribe 10% como decimal: 0.1. La parte ÷ el porcentaje da el entero: 16 ÷ 0.1 = 160. Comprueba: el 10% de 160 = 16.
